# Birko.Data.ElasticSearch.Views

<!-- spec-links: generated by Birko.Framework/spec-links.cs from docs/specs/.map.yml. Do not edit: change the map and run `dotnet run spec-links.cs`. -->
**Specs**: [views-and-aggregation](../Birko.Framework/docs/specs/views-and-aggregation.md)
<!-- /spec-links -->

ElasticSearch platform implementation for Birko.Data.Views. Translates ViewDefinition into NEST search requests with aggregations for grouped queries and _source filtering for simple queries.

## Components

- **ElasticSearchViewStore\<TView\>** — Implements IViewStore\<TView\> using NEST SearchRequest. Non-aggregate queries use _source filtering with sort/pagination. Aggregate queries use shared `StoreAggregationHelper` for metric creation (`BuildSingleMetricAggregation`) and metric extraction (`ExtractMetricValues`); the GROUP BY is the view's own composite aggregation (the entity stores' builder went with TASK-878). Joins are refused (`NotSupportedException`) rather than ignored. Filters, sorts and group keys name view properties and are mapped to the source fields they select (TASK-151). A grouping view reads a composite aggregation page by page to the end, then orders, pages and counts its rows in memory; `CountAsync` counts groups. `EnsureAsync` creates only a Persistent view's own index. A nested source (`r.Sub.X`, TASK-843) is read down its path (`sub.x` in the source filter, a null object reads null) and sorts by its stored sub-field; a filter on it is refused by name (the entity translator does not translate a member below the document, SH-M142).
- **ElasticSearchViewManager** — Implements IViewManager. EnsureAsync creates a destination index for persistent views (ES lacks native views; data population requires Transforms or reindex jobs). DropAsync/ExistsAsync/RefreshAsync map to index lifecycle operations.

## Filter translation

`BuildFilterQuery` rewrites the view filter onto the document type (SH-M382) and translates it with
`ElasticSearch.ParseExpression` (passing the store's `MaxTermsCount`, TASK-851). It enforces CR-H047 itself: a supplied
filter that cannot be translated throws `NotSupportedException` instead of widening to match-all, which a `null` NEST
query would. The entity stores enforce the same rule through `ElasticSearch.ParseFilterQuery`. The view store keeps
its own copy because it translates the rewritten document filter, not the caller's lambda; keep the two in step. A
null filter still means "no filter" and yields `MatchAllQuery` here, which is this view store's own deliberate
contract for an unfiltered view.

`MaxTermsCount` (init, `null` by default) is the read index's `index.max_terms_count`: a filter's collection
`Contains` is split at it (TASK-835), passed to `ParseExpression` per call; `null` uses the process-wide default
(TASK-851).
